verdict.rationale: AMD publishes 288GB HBM3E at 8TB/s with MXFP4/MXFP6 low-precision support, and an independent architecture analysis confirms the same capacity and bandwidth. That is far more than a quantized 70B model needs on a single GPU, and ROCm documents vLLM and SGLang for serving it. missing for 10: no hands-on benchmark of a 70B-class quantized model on a single MI355X (the community benchmarks cover an 8-GPU setup on a different model), and no first-party 70B single-node inference recipe or throughput figures.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run a 70B-class quantized LLM on this GPU — published VRAM capacity and memory bandwidth that make local or single-node inference practical

citations.quote: 288GB HBM3E memory, 8TB/s bandwidth, and expanded MXFP6 and MXFP4 datatype support
MI355X offers 288 GB of HBM3E at 8 TB/s versus B200's 180 GB at 7.7 TB/s, which helps when competing models run out of VRAM.
